method_notes: Southwark community school admission arrangements 2026/27 (also printed in 'Starting primary school in Southwark 2027/28' pp20-21), criterion 5: children living nearest to the school as measured by a straight line from the child's home to the main school gate/entrance. Note (e): the LA uses the eastings and northings linked to the applicant's address, generated by its Capita pupil database; blocks of flats with a communal entrance use the grid reference of the block, with lower door numbers taking priority. Ivydale (two sites) is measured to the main gate/entrance of both sites and the shorter distance used. Tie-break: straight-line distance, then drawing lots; multiple births admitted as excepted pupils. Criteria: LAC/previously LAC, EHCP-named, medical/social need, siblings, children of permanent staff (capped per form of entry), distance. Own-admission-authority schools mostly also use straight line (to main entrance, main gate, school entrance or site centre); St Peter's CofE and St Joseph's Gomm Road use walking distance; Angel Oak's summary gives no distance criterion.

gaps: Southwark publishes allocation figures for its 28 community schools only; all 37 academies, free schools, VA faith schools and the foundation school are recorded not_published (the booklet gives only their applications received). Their methods come from the booklet's criteria summaries, not full policies (Angel Oak: no distance criterion in summary, method unknown; St Anthony's method inferred from sibling trust schools). The council table gives only 'all offered' or a furthest distance; the criterion of the last offer is not stated. John Ruskin 2025 furthest distance 12416 m recorded as printed but looks like an outlier. The 2024 table (2025/26 booklet) has duplicated rows for Rye Oak, Snowsfields, Southwark Park, Tower Bridge and Victory with different applicant counts (all 'all offered' either way) plus a closed school (Townsend) - a layout error in the source; Bird in Bush is absent from the 2024 table (not_published). 'Bessemer Grange' (tables) = Bessemer Primary (directory). PAN = 2026/27 PAN in the 2026 table / AA intake table; the 2027/28 directory shows some changes (e.g. Crawford 30, Keyworth 30). Postcodes from GIAS. Junior schools (Dulwich Hamlet Junior, St Joseph's Camberwell Junior) excluded.
